interventions.step: Verify the production build in a browser
interventions.action: Installed playwright-core in ./.scratch/browser and drove the local Google Chrome against `next start`. Checked computed --ult-* values and color-scheme on the root, a Button and the open Select popup in data-theme dark, data-theme light, system light and system no-preference, at 375px and 1280px. Also checked horizontal overflow, the empty-name error, both kinds of successful submission, list selection by mouse and keyboard, and that Escape returns focus to the Select trigger. Then inspected the order of the production CSS chunk.
interventions.reason: The guidance asks for this rendered check in a production build but names no tool to do it with.

Leave agent setup out, as init's report marks it optional
decisions.why: init leaves this optional and never creates a repository. The hosted /llms.txt and guides were read directly, so the pointer skill would have added files without adding guidance.

decisions.choice: Did not load the Figtree and IBM Plex Mono faces the theme's font stacks name, so the stacks fall back to system-ui and the platform monospace.
options: Accept the documented fallback in the stack
decisions.why: The export loads no fonts and the guidance allows the fallback. Loading the faces would pull in a third-party font host this run is not meant to use.

decisions.choice: Chose the category with a portalled Ultima Select inside an inline form, rather than putting the form in a Dialog.
options: Portalled Select (Base UI Select.Portal to body)
decisions.why: The brief allows either. Intake volunteers log donations all the time, so an inline form saves a step, and a Select portalled to body still gets the root CSS theme.

decisions.choice: Gave category Badges the neutral tone, the low-stock Badge the warning tone and the in-stock Badge the success tone. The brand accent appears only through components (solid Button, focus ring, pressed list row) and the small 'Larder' wordmark, which uses --ult-color-accent-text.
options: Neutral tone for category badges, with status tones only for stock level
decisions.why: The brief keeps the accent out of status meaning. Categories are not a status, so neutral keeps accent and the status colours each meaning one thing.

decisions.choice: Quantity uses the Ultima Input with type="number", min 1, step 1 and inputMode numeric, and is validated in the form's submit handler.
options: Input type="text" with inputMode numeric and parsing
decisions.why: The catalogue has no number-field component. A native number input gives phones a numeric keypad and the browser's own step controls, while Field still carries the error.

review.reviewer: Claude on mbp1, #774: transcript, request log, notes and production report
review.rule: An intervention is an action on the project or tooling that the guidance or CLI output did not print or link. A decision is an unresolved Ultima setup, theme or styling choice that changed the output. Product choices and documented alternatives do not count. Browser checks of the consumer application follow the guidance; rendering documentation to retrieve guidance or source would count.

interventions.action: Ran `npx ultima-design@latest init --help`. The CLI rejected it (`Unknown option '--help'`) and printed its usage.
interventions.reason: No guidance prints a help command, and the CLI does not accept one. The #810 Vite review counted the same probe.

review.notes: The agent fetched llms.txt, the install, update, build-a-screen, support and Recipes guides, and the projects, list-detail, interaction-states and product-tokens lessons over HTTP. It did not render documentation, decode a data link, extract a bundle, read CRM 01's registry source or reference the live host or another checkout. It ran init through --plan and --apply, installed the theme and components with the printed shadcn@4.21.4, imported the theme where the install guide prints, and set up ESLint by the documented project-without-ESLint path. Under the arrangement rule from #845, the app keeps `minBlockSize: '100dvh'` and its `minmax(0, …)` track templates literal in local StyleX, the breakpoint as a named constant in the screen file, and only `--app-size-content-max` in screen.stylex.ts (#845 holds). The browser check follows the printed hand step, so its playwright-core install, scripts and server port are not counted. Reading the built CSS carries out the printed cascade step. The self-reported decisions (font fallback, Select over Dialog, Badge tones, number Input, the optional agent setup) are documented options or product choices. Deleting init's setup-check preview after replacing page.tsx follows the starter comment. check, doctor, StyleX lint (0 errors) and the raw-paint scan passed. All four external production cases failed `axe-open` with `aria-hidden-focus` on Base UI's four focus-guard spans around the open Select. That is not an agent choice: Base UI's Select backdrop cuts out the trigger, this app's Category trigger lands on axe's bottom-right modal sample point at 1280x800, so axe's isModalOpen heuristic misses the backdrop and reports the guards as violations instead of the incompletes the runner reviews. Two re-measures of a copy gave the same result. No operator edited the app.
